summary: Trace crop-loss causes, assess interventions, and build a monitored reduction plan. Explore the five-day intermediate course.
lede: Post-harvest loss minimization helps agricultural extension officers and produce handlers identify avoidable losses between harvest and sale. Participants map crop flows, measure lot-level quantity and quality losses, and use cause-analysis methods to investigate contributing factors. They prioritize practical interventions with Pareto analysis and prepare monitored action plans to track progress within resource constraints.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits people who handle crop losses in daily operations or must decide which corrective actions deserve time and budget.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with crop handling, storage, or agricultural supply-chain operations is recommended. No programming is required; the exercises use operational records and calculation worksheets.
